text: しずかな　ところで　くらしたくて　この　いえを　かったの　きょうは　つりに　でかけるわ！

structure.jp: しずかな　ところで　くらしたくて
この　いえを　かったの
つりに　でかけるわ！

patterns.name: 〜たい
patterns.explanation: たい on a verb means 'want to'. Here it is in its て-form, which links it to the next part as the reason. くらしたくて = 'I wanted to live (there), so'.

patterns.name: 〜に (purpose)
patterns.explanation: に before a verb of going tells what you are going for. つりに　でかける = 'go out to fish'.

patterns.name: 〜のだ
patterns.explanation: の at the end is a soft way of saying のだ, used when explaining how things came about. かったの = 'I bought it, you see'.
